protein: Spike glycoprotein S, residues 883-1034 scanned (HR1 and central helix)
readout: Cell-cell fusion score, higher meaning higher fusogenicity
assay_method: Deep mutational scanning of S residues 883-1034 in HEK293T landing pad cells co-cultured with hACE2-expressing cells. Fusion reconstitutes split mNeonGreen2 in syncytia, which were sorted into fusion-positive and fusion-negative populations; the fusion score is the enrichment ratio between them, over two biological replicates.
remark: The reference sequence is UniProt P0DTC2, the ancestral Wuhan-Hu-1 spike, unmodified, against which all 2,886 mutation labels verify at offset 0. The assayed construct is not identical to it: it is membrane-bound S with the PRRA motif of the furin cleavage site deleted to stop S-expressing cells fusing with each other, carrying an mNG2-11 fusion for the split-NeonGreen readout, and neither the deletion nor the fusion is represented here because the paper numbers its mutations against the full-length wild type and the labels only verify that way. The scan covers residues 883 to 1034, 152 of the 1,273 positions, spanning HR1 and the central helix; the other 1,121 residues carry no mutation and rest on the accession alone. The paper states that both scores were normalized so that the average silent mutation reads 1 and the average nonsense mutation 0, but Supplementary Data 1 ships neither class -- it holds 2,886 missense rows and a single WT-coded row -- and that WT row reads 0.8239 rather than 1. The WT row is carried through as the source measured it, and wt_readout is therefore that measurement rather than the stated anchor. The paper is explicit that a higher fusion score means higher fusogenicity, so the readout increases with the protein doing what it does and needs no inverting. Note that the paper's own objective runs the other way -- it hunts for fusion-incompetent mutants that still express well -- so a high normalized-score here marks a fusogenic variant, not a prefusion-stabilizing one. Reproducibility is weaker than the expression assay, the authors reporting a between-replicate correlation of 0.61 against 0.72 to 0.79, which they attribute to the short co-culture forced by the difficulty of sorting large syncytia. Not extracted from this paper: the expression score, which is its own dataset in datasets_virus/Stability; and the Source Data file, which holds chromatography and thermal-shift traces for a handful of validated combination mutants.
